content:
Apple has recently raised prices on most of its products, but a larger wave of price hikes awaits next month, covering iPhones and other products.

The iPhone is expected to see a price increase, coinciding with the launch of the iPhone 18 series, while the Apple Watch and AirPods may also be affected.

Earlier this summer, Apple had already significantly raised prices on several products.

Macs, iPads, Apple TVs, HomePods, and Vision Pro all went up in price at the same time.

CEO Tim Cook had warned in advance that a wave of price hikes was coming, but the breadth of the increases is still shocking.

The flagship products that were unaffected in the first round of price hikes included:

  • iPhone
  • Apple Watch
  • AirPods

At the time, Apple hinted that the price hikes were not over yet. Analysts also believe that the few products that initially avoided price hikes will soon face increases.

Now, with the September iPhone 18 launch event approaching, expectations of an iPhone price hike are already widespread.

The iPhone 18 Pro is reportedly expected to start at between US$1,299 and US$1,399, compared with the iPhone 17 Pro's price of US$1,099.

Apple typically lowers prices on older iPhones when new models are released, but this year older models are expected to keep their prices unchanged, or possibly even see slight increases.

The Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 are also candidates for price hikes, as the AI-driven memory crunch will also affect Watch components.

Lastly, AirPods may also see price increases. Compared with the iPhone and Apple Watch, the likelihood of an AirPods price hike is lower, as they should not be heavily impacted by rising memory and storage costs.

However, if Apple intends to raise prices across its entire product line, including AirPods, the September event is where we will most likely hear about it.

What price adjustments do you expect from Apple? Let us know in the comments.
